claims.location: p. 599 (PDF p. 1), abstract; p. 606 (PDF p. 8), Reproduction; Fig. 10
claims.quote: The mean fecundity was 50,678 eggs per female, with a range of 15,726-161,449
claims.conditions: 65 females collected May–June 1970 between Haverstraw and Bear Mountain, N.Y. (a 15-km reach of the Hudson estuary with limnetic–oligohaline transitions), 115.0–187.5 mm SL, age groups 2–7; gravimetric counts of ovaries preserved in Gilson's fluid; eggs = 1,697.08·e^(0.02·SL), r² = 0.39
claims.note: Mean per female, all ages pooled; an estuarine population.

notes: Useful for the Maine rows: the discussion (pp. 608–609) cites AuClair (1956, M.S. thesis, Univ. Maine) for white perch of Sebasticook Lake, Maine, at 164,000 eggs/female, and Taub (1969) for Quabbin Reservoir at 271,000 (age 3–4), lake fecundities 'at least double' riverine ones, which the authors relate to faster growth in lakes. Other values: maximum age 7; most fish mature by their second year; the first 3 years' growth was 78 % of the length reached by age 7; combined length–weight Log W = −4.743 + 3.093 Log L (SL); sex ratio 0.83 male : 1 female among 2,600 mature fish; spawning June, complete by July.
